text:
Person: Please start the wash and remind me to move it to the dryer when it ends.
Assistant: Sure. Which cycle should I use, cotton or quick?
Person: Quick wash, please. The kids spilled cheese sauce on their shirts, so use warm water.
Assistant: Quick wash with warm water. Should I start it now?
Person: Yes, now. The baby will sleep for an hour and I want the machine done before she wakes up.
Assistant: Started. A quick wash takes thirty minutes, so I will remind you at ten past nine.

Someone wants the garden watered right now.
water the garden
the lawn looks dry, can you give it a drink?
turn on the sprinklers
my tomatos are thirsty, pls start the water
The soil is as hard as a coin, so could you get the hose going?
Run the sprinklers for ten minutes, the grass smells sour and dry.
Give the roses a good soak.
If you could wave a magic wand and water the front beds, that would be lovely.
Could you please water the back garden? I will be away all afternoon and the flowers need a drink.

A television is for watching shows, news and films. Most people keep it on a desk or a stand and control it with a remote. Every day people change a few things: the channel, the volume and the subtitles. They say things like turn it down, put on the subtitles, or go back ten seconds when they miss a line. If a baby is asleep, they say mute the tv. If a spicy cooking show is on and the kitchen is noisy, they might say make it louder. Streaming apps let you pick a show from a list, and you can pause it whenever you need a break.

Mr. Brandt, a retired teacher, put his bag on the back seat of the car. The garage was dim, so he spoke up when he talked to his phone. 'Please notify me tomorrow at seven to check the tyre pressure,' he said. 'The back left one looks soft.' The assistant understood that he wanted a reminder for tomorrow at seven in the morning about his tyres. It set the reminder and read it back to him: 'Reminder set for tomorrow at seven: check the tyre pressure.' Mr. Brandt nodded and went inside for supper. The next morning the phone buzzed right on time, and he went out with the pump and filled the soft tyre until the gauge showed thirty-two.

name: set_kettle_temperature
does: Heats the water in a kettle to the temperature you choose, so it is gentle enough for tea, coffee or a baby's bottle.
inputs: the temperature you want, and which kettle if there is more than one
people say:
- Heat the water to eighty degrees for green tea
- It is snowing outside, I want hot chocolate, so get the water hot
- Make the water just warm, not boiling
- I need warm water to rinse the toothbrush cups, start the kettle
- Boil the kettle in the kitchen
- Get the water ready for my coffee

Rosa is not good with technology, and her phone often confuses her. Today she wondered how to say thank you in Italian, because her new neighbour had brought her a cake. 'I don't want to type anything,' she told the phone. 'And please don't show me a long list. Just say it.' The assistant understood that she wanted one short phrase, spoken aloud. It said, Grazie mille, and then said it again slowly. Rosa tried it twice. 'Say it double slow,' she asked, and the assistant said it again, very slowly. Then she asked it to save her neighbour's number as a new contact called Marco. The assistant did that and told her it was saved.

Mrs. Dube owns a small shop that sells fruit and vegetables. One morning a new farmer gave her his phone number on a scrap of paper, along with a box of potatoes. 'Save this number as Farmer Ali and clear the old number for Mr. Park,' she told her phone, 'because he doesn't sell bitter melon any more.' The assistant understood that there were two jobs in one sentence. It added a new contact called Farmer Ali with the number she read out, and it deleted the contact called Mr. Park. Then it said both things were done. Mrs. Dube said thank you and went back to weighing potatoes.

Dana the cook stood by the stove on a windy morning, sipping a cup of tea. She had a cold coming on. She pointed at the clock on the wall and spoke to her phone. 'Remind me to take half a tablet of my cold medicine at noon. The doctor said half, not a whole one.' The assistant understood that she wanted a reminder at twelve o'clock about half a tablet. It set the reminder and repeated it: 'Noon today, take half a tablet of cold medicine.' At noon the phone chimed. Dana washed her hands, took half a tablet with another cup of tea, and went back to her soup.

Person: Hello dear. I would like to put a picture of my new shelf on my page for my sister, because she lives far away and I owe her a photo. I promised her one last week. Could you please help me?
Assistant: Of course. Which picture should I use, the one you took today?
Person: Yes, the one of the shelf by the window.
Assistant: Got it. Who should see it, everyone or only your sister?
Person: Only my sister, please.
Assistant: A post can't go to just one person, but I can send the photo to her in a private message. Would you like that?
Person: Oh yes, that is better.
Assistant: Done. I sent the photo of the shelf to your sister in a private message.

Priya got home after a night shift, tired and in a sour mood. She dropped her motorcycle helmet by the door and spoke to the assistant. 'Pause the wifi on the kids' tablets until noon.' She yawned. 'No wait, make it two o'clock. I want to sleep until then.' The assistant understood that she had changed the time. It paused the internet on the two tablets and said, 'The tablets are paused. I will resume the connection at two o'clock.' Priya said thank you, closed the curtains and went to bed.

A bill is a note from a company that says how much you owe for things like electricity, water or rent, and by what day you must pay. That day is called the due date. People often change how or when they pay. They say pay the electric bill on the first, move the rent reminder to Friday, or remind me three days before it is due. Many people set up automatic payments, which is perfect for anyone who forgets. If a bank card is locked, you may need to unlock it before a payment goes through. Some people still keep paper bills in a box by the door, next to a jacket.

Someone wants to see how much electricity the house used this month.
How much power have we used so far?
Show my electricity use.
Did we use more or less than last month?
What does the meter say?
Does this month's bill still fit under fifty dollars?
Is the house using half as much power as it did in winter?
Tell me how often the heater has been running, please.
Please tell me how much electricity we used this week. I cleaned the whole kitchen with vinegar and the machines have been going all day.

A table booking is a way to tell a restaurant that you are coming, so a seat is ready for you. You give a name, a day, a time and how many people will eat. Most people change a booking at least once. They say make it for four instead of two, move it to eight o'clock, or cancel my table. Restaurants usually hold a table for about fifteen minutes, so people watch the clock. On a cloudy day some places close their outdoor seats, and some hide the full menu until you ask, so it helps to say if you want to sit inside or outside.

Someone wants the alarm turned on because they are leaving the house.
I'm heading out.
Nobody will be home until evening.
Lock the place up for me.
It's a warm night and I'm going for a long walk, so make sure the house is safe.
I will return at nine, so please keep the alarm on until then.
We're off on holiday, and I want to know the house is protected.
Please switch on the alarm. I have the weight of the whole week on me and I don't want to worry about the doors.
The last one out should turn on the sensors.

Mrs. Quill, a retired teacher, had to pick up some medicine from a pharmacy across town. She worried about the traffic. 'How long will it take to drive to the pharmacy on Elm Street?' she asked her phone. 'And is that faster than going by the river road?' The assistant understood that she wanted the drive time and a comparison of two routes. It said the main road would take twenty minutes, five minutes less than the river road. Mrs. Quill chose the main road. At the final turn the assistant told her to go left, and she arrived with time to spare.

Leo, a teenager, was texting his friends while a bowl of cookie dough sat on the counter. He said to the kitchen assistant, 'Preheat the oven to 200 so I can bake these.' A moment later he added, 'sry i mean 180, 200 is too hot.' The assistant understood that he had fixed the number. It changed the oven from 200 to 180 degrees and said, 'The oven is heating to 180. I will tell you when it is ready.' Leo put a note on the calendar on his phone about his mom's birthday on Sunday, and soon the oven beeped.

Mrs. Hale, a retired teacher, sat in her dim living room with her phone beside her. An alert buzzed on the table. It was a missed call from her cousin Ben. She picked up the phone and said, 'Call Ben.' The assistant understood that she wanted to ring her cousin back. It found Ben in her contacts and started the call. After a few rings he answered, and they talked for half an hour about the garden. When they were done, Mrs. Hale said, 'Hang up,' and the assistant ended the call.

Someone wants a recipe changed to feed more people.
Double the recipe.
Make this for eight instead of four.
There are ten of us tonight, so how much of everything do I need?
Scale it up to feed twelve.
Can you change the amounts for a bigger group?
I need to feed twice as many people as the recipe says.
Would you mind changing this recipe so it makes enough for ten? Guests are coming to watch the game on television, and I only have a big square pan.
Please work out the new amounts and record them in my notes.

Person: I need to wash my work shirts. Use less soap this time.
Assistant: Sure. Which machine should I use, the big one or the small one?
Person: The big one. I spilled my meal sauce on a shirt, and I wear a sharp suit tomorrow, so it has to come out.
Assistant: Understood. Should I use a stain cycle, or a normal cycle with half the soap?
Person: Stain cycle, with half the soap.
Assistant: Stain cycle with half the soap. I will start it now.

name: check_water_temperature
does: Tells you how warm the sea or pool water is by reading a network of sensors near the beach.
inputs: the beach or pool name, and the time if it is not now
people say:
- Is the water too cold to swim?
- Can the kids go in without a wetsuit?
- Talk me through how warm the sea is today
- What is the temperature at the pool?
- Is the lake warmer than yesterday? Update it automatically if it changes

When you shop, sizes tell you if something will fit. Clothes have small, medium and large, and furniture is measured in centimeters, like how wide a table is. When you order something online, it has to travel from a shop to your home, which can take a few days. People change things about an order all the time. They say send it to my work, make it a size bigger, or return this one. Some shops set a maximum number of days for a return, so people ask when is the last day to send it back. Delivery apps show where your package is.

Someone wants the alarm to be louder.
Make the alarm louder.
Turn it up a bit.
I can't hear the siren from the garden.
Please make it twice as loud.
I'm a light sleeper, but even I missed it last night, so raise the volume.
It should be heard from the street, even from the cinema next door.
Crank it up as high as it goes. I would pay for a louder one if I had to.
Set the siren to the top level.

Units are the names we give to measurements. We use them for lengths, weights and temperatures. A tv is measured in inches, a train goes sixty miles an hour, and a bag of raw flour weighs a kilogram. Different places use different units, so people often need to change from one to another. They say how many ounces are in a cup, how far is ten miles in kilometers, or what is twenty degrees Celsius in Fahrenheit. This matters most when you cook or travel. A recipe from another country may use grams, while your scale shows ounces.

Person: Lock the front door and open the garage, please.
Assistant: Sure. Which garage door should I open, the left one or the right one?
Person: The left one. I need to carry the salad to the car for the picnic.
Assistant: Locking the front door now, and opening the left garage door. Do you know if you want it open all day?
Person: Only for ten minutes. The weather is lovely, but I don't want the dog to run out.
Assistant: I will close it in ten minutes.

When a pet goes missing, neighbours often help each other. A lost pet notice is simple. You type the pet's name, what it looks like, where it was last seen and a phone number. Then you send it to the neighbourhood group or put it on a local board. People change the notice when they have news. They say add a photo, change the number, or take it down because he's home. Children often help look and may even scrape a knee while running around the park. When the pet is found, a short message to say thank you means a lot.

name: cool_room
does: Lowers the temperature in a room by turning on the fan or the air conditioning.
inputs: which room, and how cool you want it
people say:
- The piano room is way too hot
- I'm about to mow the lawn, so have the house cool when I'm back
- It's so hot in here that I'm getting angry
- Get the bedroom down to twenty degrees
- Switch the fan on in the living room

Someone wants a flat bike route with no big hills.
Find me a flat ride.
No hills today, please.
My legs feel heavy this morning, so something gentle would be great.
Plan an easy route along the river.
I'm still tired from Sunday, so I'd like a ride without climbing.
I don't want to push up any slopes.
Could you design a short, flat loop? My bike computer said I climbed too much last time.
Something smooth for a slow afternoon, please.

Sam, a driver, was on a break in the silent parking lot behind the depot. The team had said the wifi was slow again. 'Scan the network and tell me which devices are on it,' he said to his phone. 'I don't want to change any passwords or reset anything. I just want to know who is connected.' The assistant understood that he wanted a list of devices and no changes. It scanned the wifi and said there were nine devices, including two phones and a printer it didn't know. Sam thanked it, wrote the names down and told the team.

Person: Hello. I want to put a photo up tomorrow at seven in the evening. We will celebrate my husband's birthday.
Assistant: Happy early birthday to him. Which photo would you like to post?
Person: The snowy one from the garden, with the smoke from the grill.
Assistant: Found it. Should I post it at seven tomorrow for everyone to see, or only for your family?
Person: Everyone, please. Can you also tell me how many people liked it?
Assistant: I can't tell you that before it is posted, but I can show you the likes after it goes up.
Person: Oh, of course. Please post it, then.

Ana, an office worker, sat down in the dim office on a Monday morning and her nose began to itch. The highway outside was busy and the air smelled like smoke. 'Turn on the air purifier and close the window by my desk,' she said, 'because I can't breathe well.' The assistant understood that she wanted two things in one go. It switched on the purifier at a medium speed and shut the smart window beside her desk. Then it said, 'The purifier is running. I closed the window.' After a few minutes the air felt fresh and Ana began her work.

Person: Play my slow songs for the shop tomorrow at nine.
Assistant: Sure. Which playlist do you mean, Evening Slow or Quiet Piano?
Person: The one with the old songs that make customers cry a little. I think it has a picture of a home on the cover.
Assistant: That sounds like Evening Slow. Should it start playing at nine tomorrow morning?
Person: Yes, and keep it low.
Assistant: I can set a low volume. I can't play it in the shop speakers and in the back office at once, though. Which one do you want?
Person: Just the shop.

Person: Pay for my parking until tomorrow at seven. I'm in a hurry.
Assistant: Sure. Which car is it?
Person: The blue one, I'll be away from it all night. I'm sleeping at a hotel, in a nice bed for once.
Assistant: Sounds good. I need the plate number to fill in the form.
Person: It is K7 4821.
Assistant: Thank you. Parking until seven tomorrow morning costs eleven dollars. Should I pay with your usual card?
Person: Yes, go.

Mia, a student, wanted a quiet place to study before her exams. She spoke to her phone while she packed her black jacket. 'Book me a room at the Lakeside Hotel for two nights, starting Friday.' She stopped and then said, 'Sorry, three nights, I want to stay until Monday.' The assistant understood that she had fixed the length of the stay. It changed the booking to three nights, from Friday to Monday, and told her the check-in time was three o'clock. Mia said thanks and zipped up her bag.

Tom, a driver, waited outside the airport with a pot of hot coffee in the cup holder. His sister was flying in from far away. 'When does Flight 482 land?' he asked his phone. 'Is it late?' The assistant understood that he wanted the arrival time and any delay. It said, 'Flight 482 is delayed by twenty-five minutes and will land at ten past six.' Tom finished his coffee, said thanks, and moved the car to the waiting area. He asked the assistant to alert him when the plane had landed, and it did.

Mrs. Ellis, a retired teacher, sat at her kitchen table with a cart of groceries still unpacked by the door. She felt scared of making a mistake with her money. 'Excuse me,' she said to her phone, 'could you kindly move fifty dollars from my savings account to my checking account? I need to pull some cash out later to pay the gardener, and I would like to be sure it is there.' The assistant understood that she wanted a transfer between her own accounts. It moved fifty dollars and said her checking account now held two hundred and ten dollars. Mrs. Ellis smiled and unpacked the cart.

Person: Run the robot vacuum at six tonight.
Assistant: Okay. Which floor should it clean, the shop floor or the back room?
Person: The shop floor. Wait, I mean seven, not six. The last customers leave at half past six.
Assistant: Changed to seven. There is a note that its filter needs cleaning. Should I remind you?
Person: Yes, tomorrow. Also, the luggage by the door might block the wide aisle. Can it move the boxes?
Assistant: No, I can't move boxes. Please put them aside before seven.
Person: Will do.

Jun, an office worker, stood in the loud lobby of her building, a parcel under her arm. She had designed the poster for a film night at the cinema across the road, and now she had to mail the prints. She said to her phone, 'I'm all out of stamps and this parcel needs to go today.' The assistant understood that she needed a place to buy stamps and send a parcel. It found the post office two streets away, told her it closed at five thirty, and showed the way. Jun thanked it and set off.

Someone wants to move a doctor's appointment to an earlier time.
Move my appointment up.
Can I see the doctor sooner?
Make it an hour earlier, please.
Email the clinic and ask for something before noon.
Is there a spot earlier in the day?
I'd like to be seen at least half an hour before the time I have now.
This is top priority for me, so could you please ask the clinic to find a slot closer to today?
Let my family group know that I am going in earlier.

name: share_screen_to_room
does: Shows what is on your laptop on the big screen in a meeting room, so everyone can see it.
inputs: which room, and which laptop or window to share
people say:
- Put my slides on the big screen
- Hook my laptop up to the room display
- Things are heating up, so show the chart to everyone
- I'm comfortable sharing just this window
- Let the whole team see my screen

name: find_bike_route
does: Finds a bike route for a ride, with the length, the hills and where to stop.
inputs: where you start, how far or how long you want to ride
people say:
- I want a ride for about an hour
- Write the route on a sheet I can print
- I'm working from home today, plan a quick lunch ride
- Move me away from the busy roads
- Is there a loop from the park that is not too steep?
- Where can I ride safely with the kids?

Noor had just woken up and her eyes were still half closed. 'Tell me my balance and email me last month's statement,' she mumbled to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted two things at once. It said her main account had three hundred and forty dollars. Then it sent an email with the statement to her address. 'Do you want me to tag the big rent payment so you can find it later?' it asked. Noor smiled. Her savings were still far from her goal, but she was glad to see the number. She said yes and went to make breakfast.

A birthday is a day each year when people celebrate being born. Friends and family give cards and gifts, and many people blow out candles on a cake, even when the wind comes in through the window. A good gift is something the person likes, and many people set a minimum and a maximum price. People use an assistant to remember dates and to find ideas. They say save the date of Dad's birthday, remind me a week before, or suggest a gift for a ten-year-old who likes drawing. Some change the date, saying move the party to Saturday.

name: scan_front_door_camera
does: Looks at the front door camera and tells you what or who is there.
inputs: which camera, and how far back in time to look
people say:
- Who is at the door?
- Is there a package on the step?
- Check the top of the stairs camera for me
- Any idea who rang the bell ten minutes ago?
- Has anyone been on the porch since lunch?

Mr. Ferris, a retired teacher, was careful about locking up at night. He sat down with a document from the alarm company beside his tea and spoke to the smart lock. 'Lock the front door every night at ten, starting tomorrow at seven in the evening,' he said, 'and increase the volume on the doorbell, please. I can't hear it from the garden.' The assistant understood that he wanted a nightly lock time and a louder bell. It set the door to lock at ten each night and turned the doorbell volume up by two steps. Then it read the plan back to him.

A flight is a trip by plane, and a flight time is the hour it leaves or lands. At the airport, a board shows each flight, its gate and whether it is on time or delayed. Gates can change, so people check often. Someone running late might jog to the gate. When they get on the plane they take a deep breath and relax. People ask for changes or news in simple words, like is my plane late, which gate is it, or tell me when it lands. If a family member is waiting at home, they ask the same thing.

Person: whats for dinner this week
Assistant: I can make a plan. Do you want five dinners or seven?
Person: 5. no wait, 6, my brother's home sunday
Assistant: Six dinners. Any food you don't eat?
Person: no fish. its snowy and cold so soup is good
Assistant: Great. I will put soup on two nights, and add pasta, rice and chicken. Should I also make a shopping list?
Person: yes, and tell me when the oven is done on tuesday. i walk in at six
Assistant: I can't read the oven sensor from here, but I can remind you at six. Shall I do that?
Person: ok

On a hot day, a fan or an air conditioner helps keep a room cool. The fan moves the air around, and the air conditioner takes the heat out of it. Most people set a number for the room, and an average choice is about twenty-two degrees. They change it with simple words, like make it cooler, turn it down two degrees, or let the fan run all night. Some people say it is too stuffy when they want fresh air. On Thursday evenings, when the heat peaks, many people start the cooling early so the room is ready when they get home.

Mrs. Wells is not good with technology, so she did not know how to book a taxi. She was staying inside because of the rain. 'I need a car to the dentist tomorrow at seven in the morning,' she said to her phone. 'And I have to print the form first, so please make it early enough.' The assistant understood she needed a ride at seven tomorrow. It booked a taxi to pick her up at her front door and said the driver would round the corner at five to seven. Mrs. Wells printed the form on her old printer and put it in her bag.

Someone wants a bike route that is about twenty-five kilometres long.
Plan a ride that is around twenty-five kilometres.
I want to ride for about an hour and a half.
Show me a loop that gets me back home after a good long ride.
I hate hills, so keep it flat, and about the same length as last Saturday.
It's a crispy cold morning and I want a ride that fills the time before lunch.
Find me something that is not too short and not too long.
Could you please suggest a route of about twenty-five kilometres? I want to get ready for the charity ride next month.

In many homes, children have rules about screen time, which means how long they can use a tablet or a tv. Some digital tools help parents set limits. A parent might say stop the tablet at six, give her ten more minutes, or only allow homework apps until dinner. When the time is up, the screen goes dark, and the child can move on to a game or a bedtime story. Parents also change chores and school runs. They say move the pickup to four o'clock, remind Sam about the trash, or tell me when homework is done.
